key_insight: Flex4DHuman shows that dense, synchronized multi-view videos of a moving person can be generated without skeletons, depth, normals, or other explicit geometry priors. It uses only relative camera-pose conditioning to reconstruct 4D human motion more flexibly than prior methods.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing dynamic humans in 4D from a monocular or sparse multi-view video when detailed geometry priors are unavailable or inconvenient to obtain.
method: Uses a multi-view video diffusion model to synthesize synchronized dense multi-view human videos from limited input views.
Conditions generation with relative camera-pose positional encoding instead of explicit priors like skeletons, depth maps, normals, or rendered target-view geometry.
Learns to exploit camera relationships to generalize across viewpoints while preserving temporal consistency in dynamic human motion.
impact: This matters because it lowers the barrier to high-quality 4D human reconstruction, making the pipeline simpler and less dependent on hand-engineered intermediate representations. For practitioners, it offers a more flexible and potentially more scalable way to build multi-view human capture and novel-view synthesis systems.

paper_title: Flex4DHuman: Flexible Multi-view Video Diffusion for 4D Human Reconstruction
paper_authors: Jen-Hao Cheng, Yipeng Wang, Hao Zhang, Gengshan Yang, Jenq-Neng Hwang
